brief: A planter of four cells with a water pipe running through the bases to feed every cell.

requirements.evidence: Four full hex bases at (0,0), (1,0), (1,1), (2,1) on level 0, connected into one body (no loose-body warnings). The bases are open-topped cells, but I could not add soil bins: every bin offer (drained, PVC-bore, plain, half-depth) was refused with MESH_CLASH against the pipe fittings running through the cell centres. So the build is a four-cell base frame without containers.

requirements.requirement: Water pipe running through the bases to feed every cell
requirements.evidence: One run (run:run-1) starts at (0,0), enters from edge 3, and passes through (1,0), (1,1) and (2,1), so its bore passes through all four cells. The route is a zigzag because adjacent-edge bends and a loop through the 2x2 block were refused by the router. Run mode was left at its default; I did not confirm it is set to potable.

finish.summary: The build has four connected hex bases in a zigzag (0,0),(1,0),(1,1),(2,1) with one pipe run passing through all four. check_build reports meshClash clear and no rule errors; the only remaining items are info-level open cap faces. The planter is incomplete: no soil bins fit because the pipe clashes with every bin type I tried, so the cells are open frames rather than containers.

notes: 1 run IRRIGATION: non-potable supply. Corners are flexible hose, glued into Sch 40 sockets, one coupling wherever hose meets rigid pipe.
cuts: buy 1 x 10 ft 3/4 in Sch 40 PVC pipe, OD 26.67 mm (US). Metric 25/32 mm pipe does not fit.
buy 1 x 25 ft 3/4 in FLEXIBLE PVC, IPS, OD 26.67 mm (US), glues into Sch 40 sockets
- flexible legs are pool/spa grade hose: irrigation only, NOT potable and not for indoor plumbing
- glue with Weld-On 795 flexible-PVC cement and P-68/P-70 primer, not ordinary rigid cement
- keep every bend clear of its glued socket: the joint fails long before the pipe does
- fit a BACKFLOW PREVENTER at the hose bib: this system is a cross-connection without one
- fit a 25-40 psi PRESSURE REGULATOR at the inlet
- drain the system before it freezes
